name: AnNIXion Influence Operation Report

fields.label: Report Title
fields.default: Influence Operation Analysis

fields.label: Client
fields.default: TODO Client Ltd

fields.label: Campaign / Subject
fields.default: TODO the campaign, narrative or network under analysis

fields.label: Reference
fields.default: ANX-INFL-0000

fields.label: Classification
fields.default: TLP:AMBER

fields.label: Bottom Line Up Front
fields.default: TODO: what is happening, who appears to be doing it, how coordinated it is, and whether it is working — in three sentences, before any method.

fields.label: Campaign Status
fields.default: Active

fields.label: Assessed Coordination
fields.default: Undetermined

fields.label: Confidence & Caveats
fields.default: TODO: what would change these judgements, and what the data cannot show. Platform data is partial by construction — say so here rather than implying a completeness the collection does not have.

fields.label: Intelligence Requirements
fields.default: TODO: the questions this analysis answers, numbered so findings can cite them.

fields.label: Scope
fields.default: TODO: platforms, languages, accounts, hashtags and the observation window.

fields.label: Legal & Ethical Basis
fields.default: TODO: the authorisation for this work; the lawful basis for processing personal data about account holders; the platforms' terms as they apply to research accounts; and the line this analysis does not cross — naming private individuals as actors on inference alone.

fields.label: Limitations
fields.default: TODO: deleted content, private accounts, closed platforms, API restrictions, language coverage, and anything inferred rather than observed.

fields.label: Approach
fields.default: TODO: how the campaign was found, scoped and sampled, and how coordination was tested rather than assumed.

fields.label: Coordination Indicators Used
fields.default: TODO: the indicators applied — co-timing, identical or near-identical text, shared infrastructure, account creation clustering, posting rhythm, follower overlap — and the threshold at which each was treated as meaningful.

fields.label: Persona OPSEC
fields.default: TODO: how the research accounts were created and separated — infrastructure, browser profile, identity material, payment, and what the subject could have observed. Record disposal as well as creation.

fields.label: Tooling & Data Sources
fields.default: TODO: collection tooling, platform APIs, archives, and how volumes were counted.

fields.label: Overview
fields.default: TODO: what the campaign is, when it began, and how it has developed.

fields.label: Framing & Techniques
fields.default: TODO: the devices in use — fabrication, selective truth, decontextualised imagery, impersonation, forgery, manufactured grassroots support, hijacked hashtags — with examples rather than labels alone.

fields.label: Synthetic & Manipulated Media
fields.default: TODO: generated or altered images, audio and video; what the provenance analysis showed; and what remains unestablished. Note the absence of evidence of manipulation is not evidence of authenticity.

fields.label: Overview
fields.default: TODO: the shape of the network — clusters, bridges, and the accounts that actually move reach as opposed to those that merely post.

fields.label: Automation & Inauthenticity
fields.default: TODO: what indicates automation and what merely indicates enthusiasm. State the limits: posting volume alone does not make an account a bot, and calling a real person's account automated is a claim with consequences.

fields.label: Supporting Infrastructure
fields.default: TODO: domains, hosting, mail, link shorteners, registration patterns and anything shared across clusters.

fields.label: Reach
fields.default: TODO: volumes, timeline and the platforms that carried the campaign — with the distinction between posted, delivered and engaged-with made explicit.

fields.label: Amplification Path
fields.default: TODO: how material travelled — which accounts, outlets or communities carried it out of its origin, and whether any of that amplification was authentic.

fields.label: Assessed Impact
fields.default: TODO: effect on the client — brand, staff, customers, counterparties, regulatory exposure. Be careful here: visibility is not persuasion, and a campaign with large numbers and no behavioural effect should be reported as such rather than inflated.

fields.label: Impact on Staff
fields.default: TODO: individuals targeted, harassment observed, and the duty of care that follows. This is a safety matter before it is a communications one.

fields.label: Assessment
fields.default: TODO: who is assessed to be behind the campaign, at what confidence, and on what evidence. Separate capability, infrastructure and motive, and never present convergent circumstantial indicators as proof.

fields.label: Alternative Explanations Considered
fields.default: TODO: the innocent and the coincidental — a genuine grievance, a marketing campaign, a single prolific user, an unrelated network recycling the hashtag. An analysis that never considered these is not an analysis.

fields.label: Attribution Caveats
fields.default: TODO: what is deliberately not claimed, and why. Attribution to a named person or organisation is a statement with legal weight.

fields.label: Summary
fields.default: TODO: the shape of the response, and its sequencing.

fields.label: Platform Reporting & Escalation
fields.default: TODO: what has been reported, through which route, with what result, and what remains. Include the evidence package each platform requires.

fields.label: Communications Posture
fields.default: TODO: whether to respond publicly at all. Amplification is the most common self-inflicted harm in these cases; say plainly when the recommendation is to do nothing visible.

fields.label: Monitoring
fields.default: TODO: the indicators to keep watching, thresholds for re-escalation, and who owns it.

fields.label: Resilience
fields.default: TODO: what reduces exposure next time — executive footprint, verification of official channels, staff briefing, and a prepared response path.

fields.label: Legal & Regulatory Options
fields.default: TODO: preservation of evidence, referral routes, and notification obligations where staff or customers are targeted.

fields.label: Indicators
fields.default: TODO: accounts, handles, domains, URLs and hashes, in a form that can be ingested.

fields.label: Collection Log
fields.default: TODO: what was collected, when, by which persona, and how it was preserved — content is deleted, and an unpreserved observation cannot be defended later.

fields.label: Confidence & Grading Scheme
fields.default: Confidence describes the analysis: *high* where judgements rest on corroborated evidence from reliable sources, *moderate* where the evidence is credible but incomplete, *low* where it is fragmentary or the sources are untested. Sources are graded separately on the Admiralty scale — a letter for the source (A–F), a digit for the information (1–6).

fields.label: Glossary
fields.default:
**Coordinated inauthentic behaviour** — accounts acting together while misrepresenting who they are.

**Astroturfing** — manufactured grassroots support.

**Sock puppet** — an account operated under a false identity, by us as well as by them.

**Hashtag hijacking** — redirecting an existing conversation to carry a different message.

finding_fields.label: Summary
finding_fields.default: TODO: what this element is, in two sentences.

finding_fields.label: Detail
finding_fields.default: TODO: what was observed, where, over what period, and how it was corroborated.

finding_fields.label: Evidence
finding_fields.default: TODO: captures, archive links, hashes and timestamps — preserved, because this content gets deleted.

finding_fields.label: Assessment
finding_fields.default: TODO: what this element achieves for the campaign, and what it does to the client.

finding_fields.label: Recommendation
finding_fields.default: TODO: report, monitor, respond or ignore — and who owns it. Saying 'ignore' is a legitimate recommendation and often the right one.

Handling

This assessment was produced for {{ report.customer_name }} and is released under the marking {{ report.classification }}. It makes assessments about the authenticity of accounts and, where the evidence supports it, about who operates them. Those are claims about people: handle the report as personal data, and do not repeat its attributions outside the recipients agreed with the client.

Judgements carry explicit confidence. Where this report says an account is likely inauthentic, it means the indicators are consistent with coordination and not that inauthenticity has been established. Nothing here should be used to take action against a named individual without independent verification.
